bug_semantics: SRS accepts an unauthenticated RTMP publisher when vhost security is absent or disabled. A remote client on TCP/1935 can complete RTMP negotiation and a publish command without credentials; SRS returns NetStream.Publish.Start and accepts publisher traffic. Later functional media fanout permits content injection, stream-name occupation, and resource/bandwidth abuse. The referenced reporter PoC uses connect -> createStream -> publish and treats NetStream.Publish.Start as confirmation. The public report expressly says this is missing authentication/insecure default configuration, not memory corruption or code execution; therefore the NVD/GHSA arbitrary-code-execution wording is not supported by its cited technical report or by the audited source path.
flaw_origin: The smallest causal BIC is 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972. It is the first commit that decodes the RTMP publish command, receives the FMLE publish request, and emits onFCPublish/onStatus NetStream.Publish.Start without an authentication decision. Its parent had only preliminary releaseStream/FCPublish negotiation and rejected the resulting publisher type in SrsClient's switch. Follow-on commits made the accepted publisher fully useful: ed371d6e7e6e03415865d032a59c41c410ac58fe integrated the publish service loop, 940d2f02eb6149fcd93b2a6e338cf8bbf2484e56 connected audio/video to a source, 150489af51ebc26551b69808b4d750fb2f557e43 implemented working consumer queues/fanout, and 359c7da19ba1fc95be0a0a46ba3ccb9bc7d8de74 added the direct createStream -> publish path used by the published PoC. Commit 75f2607685814b86ad030df703834cf06f91447f later added optional allow/deny security, but deliberately preserved the already-vulnerable default (security off means allow all), so it is mitigation history rather than the BIC.
ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file -p 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972` shows one parent, author and committer `winlin <winterserver@126.com>`, and only the message `support fmle publish. fix bug of rtmp chunk stream.` There is no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailer, AI/bot identity, or other AI marker in the BIC commit object.
evidence: Advisory boundary: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fchr-h2rx-xx6p lists Affected versions: Unknown and Patched versions: Unknown while its prose says `<v5.0.213`; https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-68004 repeats that prose. The cited report at https://github.com/xuwu-xuwu/CVE-2026-68004/blob/main/CVE_Report_SRS_Unauth_Publish.md says security disabled causes SrsSecurity::check() to return OK, reports successful unauthenticated publish on both 4.0.268 and 5.0.213, and characterizes the issue as missing authentication/insecure defaults rather than code execution.

Attack path: https://github.com/xuwu-xuwu/CVE-2026-68004/blob/main/poc_srs_unauth_publish.py sends connect, createStream, then publish on message stream 1 with no credential and declares success only when the response contains `NetStream.Publish.Start`.

BIC diff: `git show --format=fuller --stat 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972` identifies the 2013-10-22 single-parent commit. `git diff e598616e14e4875bc5c7fcaf3ad981e7c992753e 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972 -- trunk/src/core/srs_core_protocol.cpp trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp` shows addition of `RTMP_AMF0_COMMAND_PUBLISH`, `SrsPublishPacket`, receipt of the publish packet, and both onFCPublish/onStatus `NetStream.Publish.Start` responses, with no authentication check.

Direct parent absence: `git show e598616e14e4875bc5c7fcaf3ad981e7c992753e:trunk/src/core/srs_core_client.cpp` shows the post-identification switch handles only `SrsClientPlay` and sends every other type to `ERROR_SYSTEM_CLIENT_INVALID`; the parent `identify_create_stream_client` recognizes only play and its FMLE helper stops after preliminary createStream/FCPublish negotiation. The BIC diff is the first point where a publish command is consumed and Publish.Start is returned. Thus the parent does not contain an accepted RTMP publish operation.

History cross-check: `git log --all --reverse -S'RTMP_AMF0_COMMAND_PUBLISH' -- trunk/src/core/srs_core_protocol.cpp trunk/src/protocol/srs_protocol_rtmp_stack.cpp` starts at 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972; later entries are path moves. `git log 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972 -L '/int SrsRtmp::identify_fmle_publish_client/',+110:trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp` reaches 99aa8bc0879da191608ff691c8fd7c50c4d5858a for preliminary negotiation and 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972 for actual publish acceptance. This rejects later renames/refactors as the BIC.

Lifecycle/direct-PoC cross-check: `git log --all --reverse -S'identify_flash_publish_client' -- trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp trunk/src/protocol/srs_protocol_rtmp_stack.cpp` starts at 359c7da19ba1fc95be0a0a46ba3ccb9bc7d8de74. Its parent 6d385f15a7ff50d123ff84d59e5cfd362f004fa4 recognizes only play after createStream, while 359c7da19ba1fc95be0a0a46ba3ccb9bc7d8de74 adds SrsPublishPacket recognition, SrsClientFlashPublish, and the Publish.Start response. This is the later extension matching the reporter PoC, not the earlier root BIC for unauthenticated RTMP publishing generally.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972 --sort=version:refname` begins with v0.1.0; `git rev-parse v0.1.0^{}` returns 5d1d0ff8bbfbf466b1eec3556f58b7d7ac4da1be, which contains the BIC. The direct createStream/publish extension first appears in v0.2.0: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 359c7da19ba1fc95be0a0a46ba3ccb9bc7d8de74 v0.1.0^{}` fails and the same command against v0.2.0 succeeds.

No closing fix: tag v5.0-r3 resolves to 313913737f13f97d9816dbc3d729e7bcd454a531 and contains the BIC. `git show v5.0-r3:trunk/src/app/srs_app_config.cpp` at get_security_enabled has `static bool DEFAULT = false`; `git show v5.0-r3:trunk/src/app/srs_app_security.cpp` has `if (!...get_security_enabled(...)) return err; // OK`. The tagged default config has no security block. Clone HEAD b0d775a316046d4dd1ed87c0f0a9871c614f56f8 (v8.0.30) retains the same false default and allow-all early return, so the cited 5.0.213 release is not a fixed boundary and the behavior remains unpatched in audited history.

Rejected fix candidate: 999514770481bedf2aabaa44001842bf7b0016cb (`RTMP: Do not response publish start message if hooks fail. v5.0.212`) only moves Publish.Start until after configured HTTP hooks. Its commit message says `Apart from the order of messages, nothing else has been changed`; with no hook and security disabled, publishing still succeeds. It is therefore neither fix_sha nor direct_fix_sha for this issue.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972` prints tree 963580f95ef5e44f63412938e45b0a007a4eeff5, parent e598616e14e4875bc5c7fcaf3ad981e7c992753e, human author/committer winlin, and the one-line message with no trailers or bot identity. No later commit, PR text, branch label, or fix metadata was used for the AI verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the missing authorization boundary on an accepted RTMP publish, not the later syntax of SrsSecurity::check() and not the unsupported RCE claim. Parent history matters: preliminary FMLE negotiation existed before the BIC, but the parent application rejected publishers and did not consume a publish request or return Publish.Start. Commit 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972 crosses that boundary; later commits make fanout operational and add the exact direct-publish PoC route. The 2015 security feature is opt-in and explicitly allows all when off, so it does not replace the original BIC. Neither v5.0.213 nor current audited HEAD closes the default path, and the advisory itself names no patched version. Because the BIC commit object has only a human identity and ordinary message with no AI marker, the closed attribution verdict is NOT_AI; null fix fields mean unpatched, not unknown.
remaining_gap: Unpatched in the audited public history: no fix commit, direct fix commit, or patched release exists to record. The advisory's `<v5.0.213` prose conflicts with its own Unknown patched-version field, the referenced report's successful 5.0.213 test, and the vulnerable code at v5.0-r3 and clone HEAD. Therefore fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are intentionally null; there is no remaining AI-attribution gap.
